verdict.rationale: incident.io documents an official remote MCP server that lets AI assistants query incidents and "manage escalations", plus a public REST API with an OpenAPI 3.0 spec, so an agent can handle escalation without the dashboard. The pack never documents acknowledging alerts or pages, or updating and resolving incidents, through the API or MCP, so the end-to-end lifecycle is unproven. missing for 10: documented acknowledge action via API/MCP, documented incident status update/resolve endpoint or MCP tool, independent hands-on corroboration of a dashboard-free end-to-end agent workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can acknowledge, escalate, and resolve incidents end to end through a documented API or MCP connection — no dashboard in the loop

citations.quote: Query incidents, analyze alerts, check who's on call, manage escalations, and run deep operational analysis — all from your existing AI tools.
The incident.io MCP server lets you connect any AI assistant that supports the Model Context Protocol directly to your incident data.
This is the API reference for incident.io. It documents available API endpoints, provides examples of how to use them, and covers authentication, rate limits, and error handling.
